author: gianyrox
text:
Critic plan review: REVISE, 6.0/10. Sound direction; five gaps to close before a build bead starts.

Data model (6): keep `requires` for unlock order and add a separate edge type, `uses`, in its own reviewed file (`learning/app/corpus/uses.json`), not inside atom files: `requires` feeds the unlock graph and mixing meanings would reorder lessons. Edge = {from, to, relation: tool | cognate | same-structure, evidence tokens, why (one sentence), status, reviewed_by}. Token match (118 of 185) is a candidate source only; "log", "exp" and "vectors" will over-match.

Review (5): status candidate, accepted or rejected, human reviewer (not the author model); measure precision on 100 random candidates first and stop if under 80 percent; only accepted edges ship, CI blocks rejected or why-less edges.

Engine (5): do not add kinds yet. Express root, cognate and same-math as `pick` and `match` with a `link` field in a separate links deck, so graders, the Swift port and the golden stay untouched. A link question is not an atom's applied task; exempt it from "exactly one applied per atom", and say which atom it grades.

Evaluation (4): none yet. Randomize atom pairs within each learner (mixed against blocked), outcome day-7 recall on held-out transfer items and on the math atom, with a kill rule; the beta is too small for a between-learner test.

Rollout (7): 1 edges plus review tool, 2 one slice (derivative, exp, log into physics) behind a flag, 3 evaluate, 4 Swift port only on a positive result.

author: gianyrox
text:
Critic plan review round 2: PASS, 8.0/10. All five round 1 gaps are closed (separate `uses.json`, review gate with the 80 percent precision test, links as pick and match with an exemption, within-learner randomization with a kill rule, one-slice rollout).

Before the build bead:
- Power: the kill rule needs 50 learners for 2 weeks and the beta has about 5; state the minimum detectable effect and what happens if the cohort never reaches 50.
- Define the primary metric and the no-gain threshold (an interval, not "no gain").
- Say how a link question updates the graded atom's FSRS card, and who writes the held-out transfer items so the blocked arm sees identical ones.
- Stratify the 100-candidate review by token (derivative, log, exp), and recheck precision after seeding changes.

author: gianyrox
text:
Critic plan review: REVISE, 6.2/10. Good scope; fix these before a build bead.

Data model (6): one overlay file per locale (`questions/es/01-mathematics.json`, id to prompt, options, steps, pairs, fix), structural fields (kind, answer, applied, numbers) only in the English base. CI checks: same ids, same option, step and pair counts and order (so the answer index and the seeded shuffle match across languages), and the same multiset of numerals and LaTeX. Missing text falls back to English, flagged.

Numbers (blocker): `parseNumber` strips commas as thousands, so Spanish "0,375" reads as 375. Make parsing and display locale-aware (es: decimal comma) with tests, and pick es-419 or es-ES.

Quality control (5): machine draft allowed, human reviewer per locale recorded in the review file, unreviewed text hidden; a `glossary/es.json` (term, approved translation, Polingual word id) with a consistency check.

FSRS (7): one card per atom or question, never per language; log locale in events. Side by side is display only, no extra grading.

Checks (5): `check_keys` is unaffected; `deck_voice` is English-only, so add a Spanish rule set or an explicit skip.

Rollout (7): a reviewed 20-question pilot, then the deck, behind a flag, with an error-report button and an en versus es accuracy comparison.

author: gianyrox
text:
Critic plan review round 2: PASS, 8.0/10. All round 1 fixes are in (overlays with CI alignment, locale-aware numbers first, reviewer gate and glossary, locale in events, Spanish voice rule or skip, a 20-question flagged pilot).

Two corrections:
- "One FSRS card per question" is not today's model: cards are per atom and the question rotates by review count. Keep one card per atom, locale-independent; do not add per-question cards.
- es-419 is not one convention (Mexico uses a decimal point; Chile, Argentina and Colombia a comma). Accept both forms when unambiguous ("0,375", "0.375"), reject "1,234" as a decimal with a hint, and let the learner pick the display style.

Also name the pilot's pass bar (reviewer error rate under 2 percent of strings).
